title: This Day at Thy Creating Word
description: This Day at Thy Creating Word in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Walsham How wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 127.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: This day at Thy cre-a-ting word First o’er the earth the light was poured. O Lord, this day up-on us shine And fill our souls with light di-vine.

lines: This day at Thy creating word
First o’er the earth the light was poured.
O Lord, this day upon us shine
And fill our souls with light divine.
This day the Lord for sinners slain
O Jesus, may we raised be
From death of sin to life in Thee.
This day the Holy Spirit came
With fiery tongues of cloven flame.—
O Spirit, fill our hearts this day
With grace to hear and grace to pray.
O day of light and life and grace,
Thy hallowed hours, best gift of love,
Give we again to God above!

licence: Public domain: William Walsham How died in 1897.
credits: Words by William Walsham How (1823–1897), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
